name: Atlantic Flyway Shorebird Initiative
summary: Grants to conserve and restore habitat, reduce disturbance and predation, and fill monitoring gaps for American oystercatcher, red knot and whimbrel along the Atlantic flyway, including Caribbean and South American wintering sites.

geography.label: U.S. Atlantic seaboard, gulf coast, Caribbean and South America

amount.note: Upper and lower limits are not specified.

reporting: Grantees report on metrics they choose from the programme's list in NFWF's Easygrants system.

deadline.text: Thursday, November 5, 2026, by 11:59 PM Eastern Time

status.quote: In 2027, the Atlantic Flyway Shorebird Initiative seeks projects that will address at least one of the following priorities

deadline.quote: Full Proposal Due Date Thursday, November 5, 2026, by 11:59 PM Eastern Time

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, U.S. Federal government agencies, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal Governments and Organizations, educational institutions, and international organizations.

geography.quote: This program focuses on priority shorebird sites along the U.S. Atlantic seaboard, the gulf coast and priority wintering sites for the focal species, including portions of the Caribbean and South America.

access.quote: All application materials must be submitted online through National Fish and Wildlife Foundation's Easygrants system.

amount.quote: The majority of awards under this program will fall in the $75,000 to $200,000 range.

co_finance_required.quote: A minimum of a 1:1 non-federal match of cash and/or in-kind services is required

reporting.quote: has a list of metrics in Easygrants for full proposal applicants to choose from for future reporting
